text:
Allergies:
clindamycin / Cardizem / Keflex

Chief Complaint:
Transfusion-Dependent Hemolytic Anemia

History of Present Illness:
___ is a ___ year old male with a past medical history
notable for CLL (dx'ed ___, pancreatic cancer (dx'ed ___
paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on sotalol and warfarin, recent
medically managed NSTEMI w/resultant infarct-related
cardiomyopathy (reported EF 25% at ___, no
characterization of valves or filling pressures) presenting as a
transfer from ___ with transfusion-refractory
autoimmune hemolytic anemia, fulminant hepatic failure, and 
rapid
AF, here for discussion of treatment options for malignancy. 

The patient was recently admitted for about 1 week at ___ with a non-ST elevation myocardial infarction and acute
on chronic anemia requiring several blood transfusions, and was
discharged 2 days ago (___) to ___.  The discharge
summary from that hospitalization is not available to me, but 
per
my discussion with the transferring hospitalist, his troponin
peaked at around 6 and his ejection fraction following his acute
coronary syndrome was 25%.  He could not tell me any details
regarding the valvular function or regionality of wall motion
abnormalities.  The patient also apparently received
approximately 7 units of packed red blood cells but his
hemoglobin continued to downtrend slowly.  He also received
steroids and IVIG for presumed autoimmune hemolytic anemia.  For
insurance reasons, he was unable to receive chemotherapy in the
hospital, and was thus discharged on ___ to ___ 
with
plans for him to follow-up in ___ clinic on ___ for cycle
1 day 1 of rituximab and cyclophosphamide.  He presented to
___ clinic and within 20 minutes into the infusion of
cyclophosphamide, he developed sudden onset of chest pain and
pressure and was sent to the emergency department.

In the emergency department at ___, his troponin 
was
found to be elevated to 0.28 but downtrending from prior.  His
ECG was not available for review.  However, other lab
abnormalities included a hemoglobin of 5.6, WBC to 249.78 (no
smear on file, though only slightly increased from prior),
platelets 101, potassium 5.7, total bilirubin 11.4, ALT 836, AST
1020, and INR 2.8.  He was admitted and the oncology service was
consulted and recommended a palliative approach to his 
treatment,
however the patient was not amenable to this plan and requested
to be transferred to ___ for second opinion.  He received 2
units of packed red blood cells with a increase in his 
hemoglobin
from 5.6->6.5.  However his liver function continued to worsen
with his INR increasing to 4.5, and transaminases elevated to 
AST
2221, ALT 1470, total bilirubin 11.4.  His hyperkalemia improved
with Kayexalate down to 5.1.  Creatinine 1.3. Haptoglobin
undetectable, LDH ___.

Vitals on transfer: T 97.4 HR 86 RR 20 BP 112/70 SpO2 on RA

Meds on transfer:
allopurinol ___ daily 
aspirin 81mg daily 
folic acid 1mg
pepcid 20mg BID 
lasix 20mg daily (home dose)
prednisone 60mg daily
sotalol 80mg BID
flomax 0.4mg daily
terazosin 5mg daily
coumadin
synthroid 88mcg daily

On my evaluation, the patient states that he feels "great." 
Overall, he does not have any discomfort including abdominal
pain, chest pain, shortness of breath, presyncope, diarrhea,
nausea/vomiting, lower extremity edema, dysuria.  Denies any
fevers.  He would like both Dr. ___ Dr. ___ to be
involved in his decision making regarding chemotherapy.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS: Pertinent positives and negatives as noted in
the HPI. All other systems were reviewed and are negative.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year old male with a past medical history 
notable for CLL (dx'ed ___, pancreatic cancer (dx'ed ___ 
paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on sotalol and warfarin, recent 
medically managed NSTEMI w/resultant infarct-related
cardiomyopathy (reported EF 25% at OSH) presenting as a transfer 
from ___ with transfusion-refractory autoimmune 
hemolytic anemia, hepatic failure, rapid AF, transferred for 
discussion regarding second opinion treatment options for 
malignancy. Has gradually and quickly decompensated during this 
admission with overt signs of hypoperfusion leading to cardiac, 
renal and hepatic failure. Has been made DNR/DNI, then 
transitioned to CMO given rapid multi-systems failure. Pt. 
Expired at ___ 15:28.

#Goals of Care:
On admission and throughout his hospital stay, Pt. is alert and 
oriented and in capacity of making own decisions. Has previously 
indicated that he would like to remain full code and seeking 
second opinion for treatment of CLL. Advanced liver, heart and 
kidney failure are likely all secondary to hypoperfusion due to 
his refractory hemolytic anemia, recent NSTEMI and cardiac 
failure. His current status was discussed with him and his 
daughter ___, his HCP). The patient elected to change his 
status from Full code to DNR/DNI, which was echoed by his 
daughter. We also discussed avoiding procedures that are likely 
to present more harm than benefit, while we focused on 
treatments that are indicated and will likely improve the 
patient's longevity or quality of life. With rapid ensuing 
multi-systems failure, the patient elected to pursue comfort 
measures only and was transitioned to CMO.

#Myocardial Infarction
#Infarct Related Cardiomyopathy
#Heart Failure
#Hypotension
#Shock, multifactorial
Patient has known history of NSTEMI at OSH that was treated 
medically with troponins peaking at 6. Is requiring recurrent 
pRBC transfusions for hemolytic anemia with evidence of end 
organ damage secondary to hypoperfusion. Unclear if NSTEAMI was 
secondary to coronary lesion or hypoperfusion in this setting. 
Unclear if patient has had previous heart failure, but recent 
echo with EF=29% (on Lasix 20mg), leading to a vicious cycle of 
hypoperfusion and heart failure. Shock is most likely 
multifactorial (cardiogenic component from heart failure, 
distributive secondary to acidemia and organ failure as well as 
hypoperfusion secondary to anemia). Was triggered ___ d/t to 
hypotension, measured at 80/40, though patient was asymptomatic 
and denied chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations or
nausea. Was given a bolus of 500ml LR and ordered for 
transfusion (See below) with improvement to BP 90/60 (MAP=70). 
12-lead ECG showed AFib with V4-V6 ST depressions, Right-sided 
V4 with ST elevations. Cardiology was consulted, appears more 
likely that this is a Type II MI secondary to hypoperfusion, 
patient was not
indicated for PCI which was likely to be harmful in his current 
condition. Per cardiology, given elevated INR, also deferred 
aspirin. Overall clinical picture is worrisome for RVMI in the 
setting of hypoperfusion. Given this picture, efforts were made 
to optimize Hb>8. Midodrine was uptitrated to improve 
circulatory
pressure. Troponins were positive but significantly lower than 
reported OSH values, CK-MB was negative and both remained 
without significant change four hours later; neither was trended 
further as the patient elected to be made CMO before.

#Acute liver injury:
#Liver failure:
Presented with elevated LFTs with pattern of injury most 
consistent with hepatocellular injury. Elevated Tbili with 
direct predomninance likely reflective of hemolysis rather than 
cholestasis. Normotensive suggesting against shock liver, 
although may be hypoperfusing in the setting of rapid AF or 
delayed response to
previous cardiac insult, as well as down trending blood counts 
and recurrent transfusions. This is probably also exacerbated by 
liver congestion given decreased cardiac function. INR is 
elevated, although he is without confusion suggesting against 
fulminant liver failure. LFTs continue to rise, suggesting
ongoing liver failure. RUQ/US without biliary dilatation or 
evidence of PVT, doppler included. HCV, HBV negative, HAV 
pending. Rapid increase in LFTs and bilirubin was noted on 
second day of admission (___). The pt. was monitored for 
increased encephalopathy, but remained oriented throughout. 
Neuro exams were non-focal. 

#Oliguric Renal Failure
#High Anion Gap Acidosis
High anion gap acidosis is explained by elevated lactate (10.6 - 
___ AM) and is most likely secondary to hypoperfusion and 
renal failure. Renal failure is also likely a result of 
hypoperfusion. Potassium has been normal and does not require 
intervention at this time. Attempted to improve perfusion with 
volume and pRBC
transfusions. Dialysis was not indicated, given the risk of the 
procedure and that patient is unlikely to tolerate it. Of note, 
renal failure likely also contributing to anemia. Electrolytes 
were monitored repeatedly until the patient elected to be made 
CMO. 

#Rapid atrial fibrillation: 
Was on sotalol as outpatient, recently down-titrated, 
transitioned for metoprolol on admission given persistent rapid 
AF and prolonged QT. Amiodarone contraindicated in liver 
failure. He was started on metoprolol 12.5 mg Q6H on admission 
and up titrated up to 37.5 Q6H, with rates 110s-120s, then 
adjusted back to 25 Q6H. Midodrine for blood pressure support 
(see above). Cardiology has
been consulted and followed. Considered dosing Sotalol and/or 
digoxin according to QT and renal function, but they were not 
indicated.

#Autoimmune hemolytic anemia
#CLL
S/p steroids and IVIG at OSH, now on prednisone 60 mg daily. 
Most likely is CLL as cause for autoimmune hemolytic anemia. He 
reportedly required 7 u pRBC on initial admission, then 2 u pRBC 
from ___ on re-presentation. Hgb 7.7 overnight on
admission, demonstrating appropriate bump. Has required 1*pRBC 
on ___ for Hb=6.8. Direct coombs positive. He received 
cyclophosphamide, however was never administered rituximab. We 
continued to trend his CBC closely to help determine the 
trajectory of his hemolytic anemia and transfused to slow down 
end organ damage given continued hypotension and hypoperfusion 
with a target Hb=8 and Plt=10 (pt. did not require PLT 
transfusions). DIC labs were negative. Prednisone 60mg QD was 
just above 1mg/kg and was continued. Rituximab was not indicated 
given the patient status. Dr. ___ oncologist 
was kept updated.

#Pancreatic cancer: 
Followed by Dr. ___. s/p 3 cycles of gemcitabine with unclear 
treatment response, last in ___ at which time required 
dose reduction. Dr. ___ visited the patient on ___, and 
was kept updated with his status.

#Supratherapeutic INR
Suspect related to liver injury. Unlikely to respond to Vitamin 
K treatment in setting of liver injury. Warfarin was held. FFP 
was not indicated.

#Hematuria
Has had blood tinged urine since ___ AM. Most probably 
secondary to supratherapeutic INR and liver failure. 

# Code Status/ACP: DNR/DNI/CMO
# Disposition:  Patient passed away on ___ at 15:28.

Discharge Diagnosis:
Expired
